gateway_checks.conclusion: unverified, nothing mismatched: in both passes all 98 rows (per gateway 26 raw-block checks and 23 full-byte checks) stayed unverified. ipfs.io and dweb.link no longer serve backend or automated HTTP clients: the full-byte requests got 429 with retry-after 900 and the service-worker notice, and ?format=raw was redirected to trustless-gateway.link, whose origin failed with 521/522/525. README.md:69's two example gateways cannot demonstrate retrieval any more; choosing the two replacement public gateways is the operator's decision.
stopped_attempts: 2026-10-17T09:22Z: stopped and discarded; with two requests in flight per gateway and 20 minutes per object it would have run for hours against gateways that refuse every request
2026-10-17T09:29Z: stopped and discarded; Cloudflare's 521/522/525 origin errors were not retried; the helper now retries every 5xx and honours Retry-After

observed: 2026-10-17T09:24Z-09:25Z: GET https://ipfs.io/ipfs/<cid> and https://dweb.link/ipfs/<cid> answer HTTP 429 from Cloudflare in under 60 ms with retry-after: 900 and the body 'This IPFS gateway is switching to a service worker gateway only. See https://gatewaychanges.ipfs.io#/ipfs/<cid> for more information.'
2026-10-17T09:29Z-09:35Z: both gateways answer ?format=raw with HTTP 301 to https://trustless-gateway.link/ipfs/<cid>?format=raw, whose origin fails with Cloudflare 521, 522 and 525
a browser-like navigation request from curl gets HTTP 403

sources.says: This is a scheduled pause. Starting September 1st the gateway steps aside a little each hour ... until it retires for good on September 21 (UTC). Please fetch this content directly from the IPFS network.

IPFS is moving beyond the sponsored gateways (25 August 2026): browser users of ipfs.io and dweb.link are redirected to the service worker gateway at inbrowser.link; backend and automated clients should run their own nodes or gateways; rate limiting has begun for hotlinked and backend traffic.
Shipyard's post on winding down its IPFS work, linked from the gateway notice

informational.note: Not the README's two-gateway evidence and not in the manifest: a read-only probe the agent added after ipfs.io and dweb.link refused every request, so the operator can choose replacement gateways. gateway.pinata.cloud is operated by Pinata, which holds none of these blocks (pin-by-CID was refused); 4everland.io is a third party.

provider_records.note: every uploaded CID is announced to IPNI by Filebase (bitswap and its HTTP trustless gateway), so any IPFS node or trustless client can find and verify it; Filebase is the only provider

gateway_probe.note: one ?format=raw request per gateway for tables/address/part-00000.parquet (bafkreiffiwfbn4nd75rnwv7t7l4qvo3oqta5jvtjg4lutxg7lrlnsihepi, 3772 bytes), 2026-10-17T09:33Z; redirects followed

results.operator: Pinata (holds none of these blocks: pin-by-CID was refused)
Filebase, the upload vendor and the only provider: a locator, not independent evidence
